ranked_recommendations: p-Me to p-CN
p-Me to p-CF2H
p-Me to p-F
p-Me to p-CONH2
p-Me to p-CH2OH
response.key_reasoning: The first three remove or suppress benzylic oxidation with increasing changes in polarity and binding risk. The amide probes the high-polarity boundary. The alcohol is a mechanistic pre-oxidized probe. p-CF3 was deprioritized because added lipophilicity could worsen solubility.
response.decisive_experiment: Parent versus p-CN in same-batch potency, human and mouse microsomal clearance, metabolite identification, solubility, and permeability. Promote if clearance improves about threefold, para-methyl oxidation disappears, potency remains within threefold, and solubility does not decline.
main_failure_modes: solid-state effects can defeat a descriptor-based solubility expectation
metabolism can shift to another site
the para-methyl can make a required hydrophobic contact
